body.statement: Corollary 1 (strictness relative to Teh--Sadeghi--Soo). For the certified input \(\mathfrak u_{\star}\) and query \(P_{Y_1=+1}(Y_3=+1)\), the sufficient graphical conditions of Theorem 3.2 of Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo are not satisfied, whereas \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) returns a rational positive separator; the table \(p_{\star}\) is an explicit admissible separator with graphwise values \(13/20\) under \(D_A\) and \(1/2\) under \(D_B\). Hence SparseSIM-ID strictly tightens that sufficient-only test on certified tied-sparsest inputs by resolving at least one query on which it is undecided.
body.proof_tex:
Take \(X=\{1\}\), \(Y=\{3\}\), and \(\mathfrak G_{\star}=\{D_A,D_B\}\). By \(\mathrm{lem{:}teh\text{-}sufficient\text{-}criterion}\), the first graphical requirement forbids a proper semidirected path from \(X\) to \(Y\) beginning with an undirected edge. Both \(D_A\) and \(D_B\) are DAGs, so neither contains an undirected edge and this requirement holds vacuously.

For the pairwise part of that criterion, in \(D_A\) node \(1\) is an ancestor of node \(3\), while in \(D_B\) it is not. Hence the relevant treatment-ancestor sets are
\[
 A_A=X\cap\operatorname{An}_{D_A}(Y)=\{1\},
 \qquad
 A_B=X\cap\operatorname{An}_{D_B}(Y)=\varnothing.
\]
Every chain component of a DAG is a singleton. In particular, the pertinent parent sets disagree because
\[
 \operatorname{pa}_{D_A}(1)=\varnothing,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{pa}_{D_B}(1)=\{3,4\}.
\]
Thus the parent-set alternative in the cited criterion fails. For its reweighted-graph alternative, the ancestral margin relevant to outcome \(3\) in \(D_A\) has vertex set \(\{1,2,3\}\) and arrows \(1\to3\leftarrow2\), whereas \(A_B=\varnothing\) and the corresponding ancestral margin in \(D_B\) is the singleton graph on \(\{3\}\). Graphs with different vertex sets cannot be Markov equivalent. The second alternative therefore also fails, so the sufficient graphical criterion is not satisfied.

By \(\mathrm{prop{:}four\text{-}node\text{-}cross\text{-}mec\text{-}witness}\), \(\mathfrak u_{\star}\) is accepted, \(p_{\star}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I_{\star}}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{16}\), and
\[
 T_{D_A,+1}(p_{\star})=\frac{13}{20}\neq\frac12=T_{D_B,+1}(p_{\star}).
\]
For completeness, the displayed formula for \(p_{\star}\) also gives its coordinate heights directly. Each of its four numerator factors is \(2/3\) or \(4/3\). The product of the four associated signs
\[
 (s_1s_3)(s_1s_4)(s_2s_3)(-s_2s_4)=-1
\]
shows that exactly one or three factors are \(4/3\). Since \(16(1-3^{-4})=1280/81\), every cell probability is therefore
\[
 \frac{2}{80}=\frac1{40}
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 \frac{8}{80}=\frac1{10}.
\]
Their reduced numerator and denominator bit lengths are at most \(6\). The defining bounds \(H\geq0\), \(d\geq1\), \(c_0\geq1\), \(m=16\), and \(r\geq1\) imply
\[
 B_{\mathrm{cert}}
 =2^{(H+1)(2d+2)^{2^{c_0(m+r)}}}>6.
\]
Thus \(p_{\star}\) occurs in the prescribed bounded rational enumeration.

Let \(D_0\) be whichever of \(D_A,D_B\) is first in the canonical graph order, and let \(D\) be the other graph. If every normal form were zero, \(\mathrm{lem{:}equality\text{-}branch\text{-}soundness}\) applied at \(p_{\star}\) would force the two displayed intervention probabilities to be equal, a contradiction. Hence at least one normal form is nonzero and \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) enters its rational-search branch. Because that enumeration is canonical and contains \(p_{\star}\), it returns a qualifying separator no later than the check of \(p_{\star}\). By \(\mathrm{lem{:}bounded\text{-}search\text{-}certificate\text{-}soundness}\), every such returned table is a sound exact-oracle separator. Independently of which qualifying table appears first, \(p_{\star}\) itself is the asserted replayable separator with values \(13/20\) and \(1/2\). This one certified query is outside the sufficient graphical region and is nevertheless resolved as nonidentification, proving the claimed strictness in decision-output coverage.
body.justification: This finite corollary turns the comparator relation into an auditable strict inclusion rather than a prose promise.
body.gap: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo give a sufficient graphical criterion and leave necessity unresolved; this certified exact-oracle instance is outside their decided region but receives a checkable nonidentification certificate.
body.consumer: A regression test for Tetrad SP and causaldag or GSP can verify that an undecided graphical case is reported as exact ambiguity rather than silently selecting a graph.
